title: Geometrically reduced fibres descend along affine inverse limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $a\in I$ and a morphism $q_a:Y_a\to S_a$ of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Put $Y_i=Y_a\times_{S_a}S_i$ for $i\ge a$, $Y=Y_a\times_{S_a}S$, and write $q_i:Y_i\to S_i$, $q:Y\to S$ for the projections [def-pc-base-change]. If every geometric fibre of $q$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced (all its local rings have no nonzero nilpotents), then there is $b\ge a$ such that every geometric fibre of every $q_i$ for $i\ge b$ is reduced. Empty sources and empty fibres are allowed; flatness is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible), Tag 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced), and literature/stacks-project/limits.tex Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible). These give the geometric-reducedness instance of Temkin §3.1 Remark 3.1.1(i).

proof.text: Write $p_a:S\to S_a$ and $p_{ia}:S_i\to S_a$ for the system projections. Define $E_a=\{s_a\in S_a\mid (Y_a)_{\bar s_a}\text{ is reduced}\}$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-constructible] to $q_a:Y_a\to S_a$. Its quasi-compactness and local finite presentation are part of the assumed finite presentation, and its base is qcqs by hypothesis. Thus $E_a$ is constructible in $S_a$.

Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] to $q_a$ and $p_a$. Since $Y=Y_a\times_{S_a}S$ with projection $q$, its reduced-geometric-fibre locus is $p_a^{-1}(E_a)$. The hypothesis says this locus is all of $S$. Hence every $s\in S$ satisfies $p_a(s)\in E_a$, so $p_a(S)\subseteq E_a$. No surjectivity of $p_a$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 0576, lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced; Tag 05FG, proof showing h(S) is contained in E.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] for the given inverse system $(S_i)$, its limit $S$, the index $a$, and the constructible subset $E_a$. All its hypotheses are present: the stages are qcqs, the transition morphisms are affine, and Step 2 gives the required image containment. It supplies $b\ge a$ such that $p_{ia}(S_i)\subseteq E_a$ for every $i\ge b$. This applies to the original system directly, so no reindexing or preservation-of-limit assertion is needed.

Fix $i\ge b$. By [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] applied to $q_a$ and $p_{ia}$, the reduced-geometric-fibre locus of $q_i$ is $p_{ia}^{-1}(E_a)$. Step 3 says every point of $S_i$ maps into $E_a$, so this inverse image is all of $S_i$. Thus every geometric fibre of $q_i$ is reduced. The same $b$ works for all $i\ge b$, as required. If the limit, a stage, or any fibre is empty, the set equalities and containments used above still hold; no nonemptiness of these schemes was introduced.
